newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-RBA official urges rewording of Banking Act.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-RBA official urges rewording of Banking Act.

text.p: Reserve Bank of Australia deputy governor Graeme Thompson said on Thursday the Banking Act should be reworded to help correct a misperception that bank deposits were government-guaranteed.
Thompson blamed the Act's reference to the Reserve Bank's duty to protect the depositors of banks for the perception among the Australian public that deposits had a "iron clad guarantee".
"I think that perception is there, and there are dangers in that," Thompson told Reuters after addressing an economic conference in Melbourne on Thursday morning.
"It's the perception of a guarantee and you can trace that perception in large part to the Act," he said. "In law, there is no gurantee, but people think there is."
He said the Reserve Bank was only empowered under the legislation to intervene to try to prevent banks collapsing.
"We supervise (banks) and the effect is to reduce the chances of failure," he said.
But, he added, "whether the Senate would be prepared to remove the depositor protection references in the Banking Act is another question."
